## Discovery & Translational Science

- **[Big Pharma]** **Triple-combination vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor restores CFTR function in complex allele** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42829305/)
  - Preclinical testing in primary human nasal epithelial cells showed that the next-generation CFTR corrector/gater combination vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor partially restores CFTR chloride channel function in cells carrying the rare L467F;F508del complex allele.

- **Novel thiazolyl-urea chemotype DFMNTU inhibits Yellow Fever Virus and host CK2** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42829118/)
  - Identified 1-[4-(2-difluoromethoxyphenyl)-5-methylthiazol-2-yl]-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)urea (DFMNTU) as a lead small molecule targeting Yellow Fever Virus replication.
  - Characterization confirmed dual activity against viral pathways and host casein kinase 2 (CK2).

- **Structural mechanism review evaluates pro-apoptotic executioners BAX, BAK, and BOK** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42828501/)
  - Synthesizes recent structural and mechanistic insights into mitochondrial apoptosis executioners BAX, BAK, and BOK.
  - Discusses small-molecule activation and inhibition strategies for therapeutic modulation in oncology and degenerative diseases.

- **Targeting DNAJB1::PRKACA in fibrolamellar carcinoma** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42828719/)
  - Summarizes the mechanistic role of the signature DNAJB1::PRKACA fusion kinase driver in fibrolamellar carcinoma.
  - Highlights emerging precision therapeutic strategies aiming to target the chimeric protein and its downstream signaling networks.

- **Differential gut-liver adaptations to dihydromyricetin and silybin in hepatic injury** [npj Aging](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41514-026-00528-w)
  - Evaluated the distinct physiological adaptations induced by dihydromyricetin versus silybin in middle-aged mouse models of alcohol-associated liver injury.
  - Identified distinct target responses across the gut-liver axis, informing natural product formulation for metabolic and toxic liver disorders.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Big Pharma]** **Post hoc QWINT analysis evaluates hospitalization outcomes for once-weekly insulin efsitora** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42829184/)
  - Pooled post hoc analysis of the Phase 3 QWINT-1, QWINT-2, QWINT-3, and QWINT-4 trials evaluated hospitalization metrics in adults with type 2 diabetes.
  - Compared clinical outcomes and healthcare utilization between once-weekly basal insulin efsitora alfa and standard once-daily basal insulins.

- **[Big Pharma]** **Phase 4 data characterizes rimegepant onset in triptan-unsuitable migraine patients** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42828704/)
  - Analyzed exploratory endpoints from a Phase 4 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of rimegepant for acute migraine.
  - Mapped the detailed time course of pain relief and symptom resolution specifically in patients for whom triptans are contraindicated or poorly tolerated.

- **[Biotech]** **Review highlights oral tebipenem pivoxil for IV-to-oral step-down in cUTI** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42828629/)
  - Summarizes clinical evidence supporting oral tebipenem pivoxil hydrobromide, an oral carbapenem, for complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI).
  - Focuses on its role in facilitating early hospital discharge via IV-to-oral transition and supporting outpatient antimicrobial stewardship.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **FDA issues PREA non-compliance letters to biopharma sponsors** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/guidance-compliance-regulatory-information/non-compliance-letters-under-505bd1-federal-food-drug-and-cosmetic-act)
  - The FDA posted non-compliance letters under Section 505B(d)(1) of the FD&C Act for sponsors that failed to complete postmarketing pediatric studies or submit deferral extensions within mandated timeframes under the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA).
  - Recipient sponsors and products include Assertio Specialty Pharmaceuticals (Rolvedon), Solstice Neurosciences (Myobloc), Heron Therapeutics (Aponvie), Bausch Health (Duobrii), and Phathom Pharmaceuticals.

## Business & Strategy

- **Oracle Model projects Italian multiple sclerosis drug expenditure through 2029** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42828703/)
  - Horizon scanning update using the Oracle modeling framework forecasts national health system expenditure for multiple sclerosis treatments in Italy from 2025 to 2029.
  - Models pipeline entry, patent expirations, and shifting disease-modifying therapy utilization dynamics to inform regional drug budget allocation.

## Public Health & Policy

- **NEJM perspective calls for participant protections beyond weight loss in obesity trials** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMp2609407?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  - Re-evaluates clinical trial design frameworks for anti-obesity medications, emphasizing participant safety, long-term health outcomes, and end-of-trial transition care beyond primary percentage weight-loss endpoints.

- **Public health frameworks for managing traditional practices in viral hemorrhagic fever outbreaks** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMp2608136?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  - Examines the epidemiological role of traditional grieving and burial customs in Ebola transmission dynamics, advocating for community-centered infection control protocols.

- **Global biosecurity and preparedness lessons from Hantavirus management** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMp2611801?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  - Discusses public health policies, pathogen surveillance networks, and international resource-sharing mechanisms required to mitigate Hantavirus threats.

- Biology & Health
    - [Oats and Mortality](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/UAxbLC5ZuYA) -- Physionic
        - Observational studies link whole-grain oat and oatmeal consumption to lower all-cause mortality and consistently neutral or improved cardiovascular outcomes.
        - Eating oatmeal two or more times per week was associated with a 21% lower risk of coronary heart disease compared to consuming it less than once a month.
        - Randomized controlled trials demonstrate that oat-derived fibers lower cardiovascular risk factors such as LDL cholesterol, supporting observational findings that adjust for healthy lifestyle confounders.
        - A suggested practical target derived from the research is 50–75 grams of dry oats consumed at least twice weekly.
